items.title: Stephen Curry could request trade from Warriors near end of his career
items.content:
The Golden State Warriors have entered a new chapter of the organization and its far from what was originally envisioned.

After losing out in the LeBron James free agent sweepstakes, the Warriors look like a team once again leaning on its veteran star. Stephen Curry’s loyalty to Golden State could change if frustrations with the organization reach a breaking point, according to Nick Friedell of The Athletic.

Golden State Warriors star Steph Curry is entering his 18th season in the NBA. AP“Now, a few months later, with little improvement to the roster, the league wonders whether Curry’s mindset will change. Speculation continues from both fans and the media that Curry may become so frustrated that he eventually asks out during the final year or two of his career,” Friedell writes. 

“But that’s still hard to envision given that he has been so consistent in both his messaging about wanting to stay with the Warriors and in expressing his love for the Bay Area.”

In 2016, owner Joe Lacob famously said the Warriors were lightyears ahead of the rest of the league. A decade later, the Warriors are entering the 2026-27 season with major question marks surrounding the direction of the franchise.

Warriors owner Joe Lacob will likely want to retain Curry for the remainder of his career. Kelley L Cox-USA TODAY SportsThe Warriors failed to give Curry another superstar to play alongside for the upcoming season. Getty ImagesGolden State’s aging veteran core can’t be the future for the team, but the uncertainty surrounding its success throughout the upcoming season is not for lack of effort. The Warriors have pursued superstars — most recently James who was the top free agent of the summer.

But the Warriors have consistently come up short.

That has put immense pressure on Curry to carry the offense night after night; and the trend looks to continue after the Warriors’ quiet offseason that was headlined by the selection of No. 11 overall pick Yaxel Lendeborg in the 2026 NBA Draft.

Curry has voiced his ongoing support for the organization, and it would be a heartfelt curtain call if he remained with the Warriors. The 38 year old is entering his 18th season in the league, but his devotion to the team appears to be as strong as ever.

Could that ever change as Curry enters the twilight of his career? Possibly.

items.title: Dillon Mitchell is officially staying with the Celtics after signing a two-way contract
items.content:
LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - JULY 14: (Editors Note: Tonal effects have been applied to this image) Dillon Mitchell #20 of the Boston Celtics poses for a portrait during the 2026 NBA Rookie Photo Shoot at UNLV on July 14, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images	Just days after questions surfaced about whether Dillon Mitchell could return to St. John’s for another collegiate season, the Boston Celtics have put any uncertainty to rest.

The team announced Wednesday that it has signed the No. 40 overall pick to a two-way contract, officially bringing one of its Summer League standouts into the organization.

Mitchell’s status had become an unexpected storyline this week after reports surfaced that the NCAA appeal process could allow the 6-foot-8 forward to return to St. John’s for a fifth season. Because Mitchell remained unsigned, there was at least some uncertainty about whether he would pursue another year in college, where a lucrative NIL deal may have awaited him.

That speculation only intensified after CLNS’ Bobby Manning noted that if Mitchell returned to school, the Celtics’ ability to retain his draft rights beyond next year’s draft wasn’t guaranteed.

Instead, Mitchell is staying in Boston.

Celtics now have 14 roster players, two on two-ways, and two training camp invites for 18 players to begin the preseason. Camp roster should grow over the next month-plus. https://t.co/iXiuX7PpSW

— Bobby Manning (@RealBobManning) August 5, 2026The athletic forward made a strong impression during Las Vegas Summer League, averaging 13.0 points, 2.7 steals and 1.3 blocks while flashing the defensive versatility and relentless motor that made him an intriguing second-round selection. He also knocked down 37.5 percent of his three-point attempts, albeit on limited volume, offering another encouraging sign as he continues to round out his offensive game.

While Mitchell remains a developmental prospect, his archetype is one the Celtics have shown a willingness to invest in. Boston has prioritized long, switchable defenders under Brad Stevens, and the organization has already seen encouraging returns from similar young wings such as Jordan Walsh and Hugo González.

— Tomek Kordylewski (@Timi_093) July 11, 2026The two-way contract gives Mitchell the opportunity to split time between Boston and the Maine Celtics while continuing his development without the uncertainty that surrounded his future earlier this week.

Mitchell now becomes Boston’s second player on a two-way deal alongside center Amari Williams. The Celtics still have one remaining two-way roster spot available entering training camp.

For Boston, the move also provides some welcome clarity.

items.title: NBA Offseason Trade/Free Agent Rumors 2026: Stephen Curry's future with Warriors, Klay Thompson update
items.content:
We're spending most of today's roundup of offseason rumors in northern and central California, but we'll bounce around a little after that. Things are quiet as the rush of summer free agency is over and teams don't have to do much now until near the start of training camp.

Stephen Curry’s future with WarriorsThe combination of Golden State striking out with LeBron James and other free agents — essentially running it back with a 37-win team while waiting for Moses Moody and Jimmy Butler to get healthy — and Stephen Curry has led to idle speculation about Curry's future with the Warriors. Would one of the most loyal players in the league actually ask out in the next couple of years to chase a ring?

For his part, Curry has only ever said he wants to play his entire career with one team, and that this summer he has worked with the Warriors front office and understands the situation. Nick Friedell of The Athletic added this in a recent report.

According to one team source, who spoke on the condition of anonymity to speak candidly about the organization's internal discussions, it's not like Curry isn't aware of what Warriors general manager Mike Dunleavy and the rest of the front office are trying to accomplish. The conversation between the star and the team has been ongoing — for years.

The Warriors have consistently pursued high-level trade targets, and that's not going to stop even though those pursuits haven't ended well recently, aside from landing Butler just before the 2025 trade deadline. The fact that they haven't landed more stars has irritated the fanbase, but the Warriors remain favorably viewed throughout the league for the way the franchise operates and spends money from top to bottom.

The Warriors are doing this the right way. What gets teams in trouble is when they strike out on big swings, then, out of desperation, overpay for marginal moves that reduce their flexibility without making the team meaningfully better. It becomes an ugly spiral.

Maybe the Warriors will land another star while Curry remains a Warrior, maybe not, but from his comments this summer, he gets the big picture.

Klay Thompson updateThere is a line of teams waiting and hoping that Dallas buys out Klay Thompson — Miami, the Clippers, maybe a reunion in Golden State — but because of all that interest in him, the Mavericks are not talking buyout and are looking for a trade, reports NBA insider Jake Fischer in a stream at Bleacher Report.

items.title: Klay Thompson could opt to return to home, if Dallas doesn't work out
items.content:
There's a chance that four-time NBA champion Klay Thompson sees his time with the Dallas Mavericks come to an end after two seasons. 

Thompson, 36, joined the team in July 2024 as a result of a six-team trade, signing a three-year, $50 million contract after spending the first 13 seasons of his career with the Golden State Warriors.

Last season, Thompson appeared in 69 games for the Mavericks and started eight. He averaged career-lows in multiple statistical categories including points (11.7), field goal percentage (39.3%), 3-point percentage (38.3%), free throw percentage (76.6%), rebounds (2.1), assists (1.4) and minutes played (21.7).

If indeed the 2026 season was Thompson's final season in Dallas, the aging sharpshooter and his agent will soon field calls from teams around the league ready for his services. He has one year left on his contract and the Mavericks owe him $17.5 million. 

They could opt to put Thompson in trade negotiations, but given the season of career-lows he's coming off of, some could view it as a risk to trade for the 36-year-old and likely give up assets. The other option would be via buyout clause in which Thompson would become a free agent and choose his destination. 

In that scenario, Thompson would have multiple potential landing spots including some familiar to him. USA TODAY Sports' NBA reporter Lorenzo Reyes wrote that two possible places for Thompson to land are the Warriors and Los Angeles Lakers.

Either of the two would make complete sense. 

Klay Thompson to Golden State Warriors?Thompson began his career with the Warriors when he was drafted in 2011. He helped them to become one of the league's dynasties, while he became a five-time All-Star, Olympic gold medalist and recognized as one of the best shooters in NBA history.

He and Stephen Curry formed the dynamic, sharp-shooting backcourt duo nicknamed the "Splash Brothers." And with Draymond Green as an enforcer, the big three would be back together again, albeit a lot older than their initial stint together. A reunion amongst them would be the full-circle moment that many want to see, maybe with the exception of rival opponents.

As Reyes wrote, "there would be no fit better for Thompson than Golden State. Coach Steve Kerr is still there. Stephen Curry is still there. Thompson knows the system intimately and the Warriors — who tied for 17th last season in 3-point percentage (35.6%) — could definitely use a shooter like him."

The Warriors might not be a championship contending team leaning on Curry and company. Adding Thompson may not move the needle in wins but nostalgia itself will provide enough energy to make due with however things played out.
